title: Compliance readiness & evidence plan - Elysian Insurance
meeting_header: Date: 2026-03-25 | Start: 15:00 PDT | Duration: 42m | Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Arjun Patel (Redwood SE), Sofia Li (Redwood CSM), Rajesh Khanna (CISO, Elysian), Nicole Park (Head Cloud Eng), Dana Morales (Procurement), Omar Ruiz (Sec Eng)
summary: Customer asked for a gap-focused SOC 2 / ISO27001 evidence plan and Trust Center access. Main asks: how to get read-only org-level reports, RBAC/SAML mapping, KMS integration options for customer-managed keys, and expected timeline for proof bundle. We agreed next steps: create a trust-center invitation for Elysian, share SOC 2 beta report (redacted), run a short evidence RACI workshop, and schedule a 30-min technical deep-dive for KMS & VPC connectivity.
topics: Trust Center access and read-only reports
Data residency and dedicated VPC/on-prem considerations
Timeline for SOC2 report and evidence handoff
transcript: 00:00 Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thank you for joining. Quick roll call, then we'll go over the SOC 2 / ISO evidence path. 00:08 Rajesh Khanna: Hi, Rajesh here. We're mainly focused on evidence delivery and who touches what, and whether we can get org level reports. 00:15 Maya Chen: Totally. Our goal today is to outline trust center access, what reports we can provide, and a realistic evidence collection plan. Arjun will jump into technical details after the high level. 00:28 Arjun Patel: Quick note — apologies in advance if the audio is a little echo-y. So starting from the audit reports: we can provide a SOC 2 Type II report covering the inference platform controls, plus our ISO 27001 certificate and scope doc. The reports are redacted for customer data but include control narratives. 00:45 Nicole Park: When you say "redacted", can we get read-only access to the raw evidence for our scoping team? We need to map controls to our internal seller — our internal control owners. 00:58 Maya Chen: We don't give raw copies of customer data, but for controls mapping we can provide: control narratives, sample evidence artifacts, and a Trust Center read-only role that exposes the compliance reports and artifacts we've been permitted to share. 01:15 Dana Morales: Is the Trust Center account separate from the Console? How do we onboard our procurement and security reviewers? 01:22 Sofia Li: The Trust Center is a separate portal. We usually invite one or more users as viewers — SSO via SAML is supported, and we can map groups to a view-only role. We'll send an invite link once we have the list of emails. 01:38 Omar Ruiz: For SAML/SCIM, do you support group sync? We prefer SCIM for group provisioning so we don't manually manage viewers. 01:45 Arjun Patel: Yes, SCIM is supported. The typical flow is: we set up a SAML connection, then enable SCIM for provisioning groups and mappings. There are a couple of attributes we expect (email, name, group). 02:00 Rajesh Khanna: Regarding KMS: we need to know if we can bring our own keys and whether they are used for data at rest across hosted and dedicated modes. 02:10 Arjun Patel: Short answer — customer-managed keys (CMK) are supported for Private deployments today and for Dedicated via our KMS integration. For Hosted, we offer envelope encryption with our managed keys, but we can support BYOK for enterprise plans — it's handled through an HSM/KMS integration. 02:30 Nicole Park: Can you confirm where the key material actually lives? We prefer our keys in our cloud KMS (AWS KMS). 02:36 Arjun Patel: Keys stay in the customer KMS when using BYOK — we store only wrapped keys and use them for decrypt ops in dedicated/private. I'll follow up with an architecture note. 02:48 Maya Chen: Note: there was a request in pre-call email about whether Redwood's log stream has full audit trails to ship to customer SIEM. 02:55 Arjun Patel: We have an audit log export feature. Logs include request ids, model version, route, timestamps, and user id where applicable. We can stream logs to a customer S3 or to a push endpoint, and we support common log formats. Retention is configurable by plan; default is 90 days. 03:18 Omar Ruiz: Is there any PII in the logs by default? We need to know redaction behavior. 03:24 Arjun Patel: Logs do not store model outputs unless explicitly enabled; by default logs contain metadata. If you enable detailed payload logging, you should plan for encryption-at-rest and separate retention. We can redact or mask tokens on ingest. 03:40 Rajesh Khanna: For SOC 2 controls mapping — we have a matrix that expects specific artifact types for CC6, CC7 — can you give an example of what you provide for monitoring and incident response evidence? 03:52 Maya Chen: Example: for incident response we provide our IR runbook, a sample incident ticket with redactions, and SOC postmortems (redacted). For monitoring, we provide metrics dashboards, uptime reports, and alerting configuration screenshots. 04:12 Nicole Park: Will auditors accept your redacted artifacts? Our internal auditor teams sometimes push back. 04:19 Sofia Li: We've worked with multiple enterprise auditors; as long as the artifact shows the control operation and is traceable to the control description, they accept redacted versions. We can also provide a letter of attestation if needed. 04:36 Dana Morales: Procurement will need an evidence delivery timeline. If we sign by end of April, when can we expect the trust center invites and the SOC2 Type II copy? 04:46 Maya Chen: Trust Center invites — we can send within 2 business days after we have the list. Redacted SOC 2 Type II report — we can share the latest copy within 5 business days after NDA/LOE signoff. 04:59 Rajesh Khanna: LOE meaning what here? 05:02 Maya Chen: LOE is the legal order/execution — a simple confidentiality addendum if your counsel requires it. We'll coordinate with Dana and your legal contact. 05:10 Arjun Patel: On control mapping workshops: we recommend a 60–90 minute RACI session where we ingest your control matrix and map Redwood artifacts to your control ids. Typically Arjun + Sofia attend as SMEs. 05:24 Nicole Park: Good. We also need to validate that RBAC in the console supports our internal roles — e.g., separation of duties between Admin, Audit Viewer, and DevOps. 05:35 Arjun Patel: The Console supports role-based permissions. Roles can be customized to limit access to billing, models, or audit features. For Trust Center viewers, it's read-only. For example, Audit Viewer can see logs and reports but cannot change settings. 05:51 Omar Ruiz: For private deployments, any additional attestation items? We run some on-prem critical controls. 05:58 Arjun Patel: For Private, we provide an architecture diagram, network segmentation docs, and an onboarding checklist. If you run on-prem, you own the physical controls, but we provide guidance for what auditors will expect (host hardening, network ACLs, patching cadence). 06:17 Rajesh Khanna: Data residency — we must ensure that tokens and prompt history for EU customers remain in EU regions. How do you handle per-tenant region pinning? 06:27 Maya Chen: We can pin a customer's data region on Dedicated and Private. For Hosted customers, region pinning is available for enterprise tiers; we can ensure processing and storage in EU gce/az for EU-resident customers. We'll add the region mapping note to the architecture doc. 06:40 Nicole Park: Any known compliance gaps we should be aware of? 06:44 Arjun Patel: One nuance: full BYOK for hosted multi-tenant flow is limited; if BYOK is a hard requirement, Dedicated or Private is recommended. Also, certain long-term retention customizations are limited on Hosted. We'll surface these as "considerations" in the RACI doc. 07:02 Dana Morales: Ok procurement question — what contract clause covers log retention and access in the event of contract termination? 07:10 Maya Chen: We have a standard data export clause; we commit to returning customer data and providing a data export package within 30 days of termination. Log export availability can be configured earlier if you enable streaming. We'll share the specific contract language. 07:26 Rajesh Khanna: Auditors often ask for a control owner contact for each artifact. Can you provide a named contact for each control area? 07:33 Sofia Li: Yes, we can supply a control owner spreadsheet — name, role, contact, and sample artifacts. We'll coordinate to ensure it's clear which artifacts map to each control id. 07:45 Nicole Park: About the workshop — who should join from our side? 07:48 Maya Chen: Recommended: your CISO or delegate, a control owner for security ops, and someone from cloud engineering. The workshop will produce a mapping CSV and a set of open evidence items. 08:01 Omar Ruiz: For evidence items that require automated pulls, can we set up cross-account S3 or an API to fetch artifacts? 08:08 Arjun Patel: We can provide signed S3 exports for some artifacts and API endpoints for audit logs; for private deployments you can access the raw stores. We'll document the options. 08:21 Rajesh Khanna: Any blockers on RACI that typically slow things down? 08:25 Sofia Li: Common slow points: getting legal NDAs in place, collecting internal control owners' time commitment, and SCIM provisioning delays if IdP owners are busy. We'll try to own the setup work where possible. 08:38 Dana Morales: Can you share a sample mapping template after this call? 08:41 Maya Chen: Yes — we'll attach a mapping template and a suggested timeline. 08:46 Nicole Park: One last technical — do you support exporting logs to our Splunk instance vs S3? 08:51 Arjun Patel: Splunk HEC endpoint support is available; we can stream in near real-time. We'll need the HEC token and endpoint details during configuration. 09:05 Rajesh Khanna: Thanks — let's recap next steps. 09:08 Maya Chen: Recap: 1) Redwood to send Trust Center invites (SAML instructions) within 2 business days, 2) Share redacted SOC2 & ISO artifacts within 5 business days after LOE, 3) Send mapping template and schedule a 60–90 min RACI workshop next week, 4) Arjun to follow up with KMS architecture doc and Splunk/HEC config notes. 09:30 Dana Morales: Will do. Thanks everyone. 09:34 Maya Chen: Thanks all, we'll follow up with calendar invites and the artifact links.
next_steps: Redwood to send Trust Center invite and SAML/SCIM setup guide
Share redacted SOC2 Type II and ISO 27001 artifacts after LOE
Deliver mapping template and schedule RACI workshop
Arjun to share KMS architecture note and Splunk/HEC config details
